title: An OpenAI-compatible stream that ends without a finish_reason is reported as a finished answer: a cut-off 'RELIANCE closed at Rs 1,4', or a blank assistant turn, with no error and no Retry
repro: Sidecar :52224 booted with OPENAI_BASE_URL -> loopback junk stub (harness/junk_provider.py). vy.py invoke copilot 'What is the price of RELIANCE?' --provider openai --bad-key --model junk-truncated -> one delta 'RELIANCE closed at Rs 1,4', socket closed, then {kind:done, finish_reason:null}, no error. --model junk-html (HTTP 200 text/html captive-portal page) -> only {kind:done}, zero text. --model junk-emptychoices (choices:[] then [DONE]) -> only {kind:done}. Same junk through the Ollama adapter (OLLAMA_HOST) -> honest parse_error frames.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/failure-inducer/50-junk-truncated.txt, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/failure-inducer/50-junk-html.txt, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/failure-inducer/50-junk-emptychoices.txt, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/failure-inducer/51-ollama-junk-ndjson-truncated.txt, sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:751, sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:830, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1485, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1499, src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:914-919, src/store/chat-history.ts:213-219, src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:1239-1250
notes: The adapter's stream loop (openai.py:751-830) yields LLMDoneEvent(finish_reason=None) whether the provider finished or the connection just died; the runtime special-cases only finish_reason=='content_filter' (agent_runtime.py:1485) and the frontend finalizes any done as success (chat-history.ts:213-219) - ErrorRow/Retry render only when message.error is set (ChatSidebar.tsx:1239). This one adapter serves OpenAI, OpenRouter (the shipped default lane), DeepSeek and xAI. Consequence: a mid-answer network drop, a proxy/captive portal or an empty upstream completion leaves either a truncated money figure presented as the whole answer or an empty bubble with nothing to click. Sibling of COD-error-layer-2-3 (length/max_tokens finish dropped) but a different trigger: no finish at all and zero output. Smallest fix: in the adapter, end-of-stream with finish_reason None -> emit LLMErrorEvent(code='truncated', 'The answer from <provider> was cut off - what is shown is incomplete'); zero content AND zero tool events -> LLMErrorEvent(code='empty_response'); the Ollama adapter already does the equivalent.

title: On the keyless search tier (no Docker/SearXNG) the chat's web_search times out at its 25 s cap because DuckDuckGo, first in the chain, burns ~41 s before Brave (0.9 s) is tried; the model then blames the network and suggests 'a lighter depth'
subsystem: search keyless rotation / agent tool dispatch
repro: Sidecar :52224 booted with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin (Docker absent -> /search/searxng/status not_installed_docker, /search/status t1_keyless, all engines 'available'). vy.py invoke copilot 'Use your web_search tool to find recent news about Dixon Technologies and cite the sources' --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b -> tool_use web_search, then the model: 'there was a timeout error ... network issues ... try again with a narrower query or at a lighter depth'. 2/2 runs (41-*, 43-*). Direct handler timing (harness/eng_timing.py, same env): ddg FAIL 20.5 s, ddg FAIL 20.4 s, brave ok 0.9 s -> total 42.5 s; other cold calls 42.6 / 45.1 / 47.4 s.
notes: The 25 s outer wait_for (catalog.py:313 via agent_runtime.py:652-666) that COD-research-retrieval-relevance-6's refute cited as the bound is exactly what turns a slow-but-working keyless rotation into a failed tool: ENGINE_CHAIN is fixed ddg->brave->mojeek (keyless.py:53), each engine gets ATTEMPTS_PER_ENGINE=2 (pacing.py:42) and DDG's own inner retries push one attempt to ~20 s (ddg.py:60,84), with no per-engine deadline, so a blocking DDG consumes the whole budget and a healthy Brave is never reached. The timeout payload's hint is the research-domain one ('narrow the query or retry at a lighter depth', catalog.py:1572) for a tool with no depth, and the model repeats it. Docker-absent keyless is the tier every user without Docker runs on (it was the operator's own state at Stage 0), and chat web search is the agent's only fresh-web path outside a research run. Nothing tells the user search is degraded: /search/status reported every engine 'available'. Smallest fix: give keyless.search a per-engine deadline that fits inside the tool cap (e.g. 6 s, no second attempt after a transport timeout) or order the chain by recent breaker history, and a web_search-specific timeout hint that names the search tier.

title: A provider that accepts the request and never streams leaves the chat on a silent spinner for up to 600 s: no stall watchdog in the adapter, runtime or frontend
repro: Sidecar :52224 with OPENAI_BASE_URL -> junk stub. vy.py invoke copilot 'What is the price of RELIANCE?' --provider openai --bad-key --model junk-hang (stub sends 200 + SSE headers, then nothing) --timeout 150 -> zero SSE events of any kind in 150 s; client gave up (TRANSPORT TimeoutError).
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/failure-inducer/52-junk-hang.txt, sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:440-445, sidecar/.venv openai 2.36.0 DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = Timeout(connect=5.0, read=600, write=600, pool=600), src/modules/chat/streaming.ts (no timer/stall logic: grep timeout|stall|watchdog|setTimeout -> 0 hits)
notes: openai.AsyncOpenAI is built with max_retries=0 but no timeout (openai.py:440-445), so the SDK's 600 s read timeout governs; the runtime emits no heartbeat/progress while waiting and streaming.ts has no stall timer. A wedged proxy, an overloaded free model that holds the socket, or a half-dead VPN shows as an indefinitely 'thinking' turn; only a manual Stop recovers, and nothing says the provider went quiet. Same class as COD-runs-durable-delegate-12 (delegate path) and COD-agent-runtime-3 (planner pre-pass), here on the foreground chat stream. Smallest fix: a first-byte/idle timeout on the adapter client (e.g. httpx.Timeout(connect=10, read=60)) mapped by humanize() to the existing 'network' frame, or an idle timer in streaming.ts that surfaces 'no response from <provider> for 60 s - Stop or keep waiting'.

title: With the network down, a valid US symbol reads as 'No price data for this symbol' on the chart and silently vanishes from the watchlist quote batch; health and search status stay green, so nothing says 'offline'
repro: Sidecar :52224 booted with HTTP(S)_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 (closed port), NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost. GET /history/AAPL?timeframe=1d -> 200 {bars:[], provider:'none', reason:null} in 3 ms (chart: 'No price data for this symbol'); GET /quotes?symbols=RELIANCE,TCS,AAPL -> 200 with RELIANCE and TCS only (AAPL dropped, no marker); GET /quotes/AAPL path -> sidecar.log 'yfinance quote failed for AAPL: PriceHistory object has no attribute _dividends' (the same text a nonexistent ticker gets); GET /fundamentals/TCS -> 502 raw 'curl: (7) Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1 port 9'; GET /health 200 ok, GET /search/status all engines 'available'.
notes: yfinance swallows the transport failure and returns an empty frame ('$AAPL: possibly delisted; no price data found' in the log), the correctness gate raises EmptySeriesError, and the Bug-2 downgrade (history.py:73-80) turns it into a clean 200 'no data' - so an outage is indistinguishable from a dead ticker on the chart, and the batch quote route discards failures by design (quotes.py:78-89) so the watchlist row just shows an em dash. IN names partly survive on cached exchange EOD (RELIANCE/KAYNES quotes came back from 'bse' cache), which makes the failure look symbol-specific rather than global. Distinct from INT-spec-135-137 (raw text for unknown symbols): here the classification itself is wrong - a transport failure is reported as absence of data. Smallest fix: have the yfinance/ccxt providers raise ProviderError(kind='network') when the underlying request failed (curl/requests connection errors are visible in the swallowed exception), skip the EmptySeriesError downgrade for that kind, and let the chart/watchlist show 'Can't reach market data - check your connection' instead of 'No price data'.

title: An invalid model id (OpenRouter 400 'is not a valid model ID') is shown as 'Something went wrong with OpenRouter - Try again or switch provider', a retry that can never succeed
repro: vy.py invoke copilot 'What is the price of RELIANCE?' --provider openrouter --model 'zzz-nonsense/not-a-model-9000:free' --port 52224 -> {kind:error, message:'Something went wrong with OpenRouter.', action:'Try again or switch provider in Settings.', code:'unknown', detail:"Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'zzz-nonsense/not-a-model-9000:free is not a valid model ID', ...}}"}. Contrast: a retired-but-known slug (z-ai/glm-4.5-air:free) returns 404 and is told 'The requested model is not available on OpenRouter - pick another model.'
notes: humanize() has branches for 402/401/403/404/429/5xx but none for 400 (errors.py:148-196), so a model-id rejection falls to the generic 'try again' (errors.py:295-300). A user who typed a custom model id into the picker (setModel accepts free-form ids; OpenRouter picks are never pruned on restore, model-selection.ts:69-75) is told to retry. The useful sentence is only in the collapsed detail. Also: OpenRouter's error detail carries the account's user_id, which the Details disclosure shows verbatim (redacted in this evidence). Sibling of COD-error-layer-2-4 (400 invalid key). Smallest fix: a 400 whose body says 'model' + 'not a valid'/'not found' -> code 'model_not_found' with the existing 404 wording.
